mainTopic: Explaining the ברייתא's definitions of the שבת domains: its wording, the desert, the punishments for carrying, and the valley as a כרמלית
overview: This amud explains, line by line, a ברייתא that defines the domains of שבת. It opens with the end of רבי יהודה's view that a לחי or קורה at each end of a public road permits carrying there; the חכמים reject this. The גמרא explains that calling the רשות היחיד 'גמורה' teaches that the חכמים do not treat that area as private even for throwing. The emphatic 'זו היא רשות הרבים' excludes רבי יהודה's other view about a public path through the posts around wells, while 'גמורה' for the רשות הרבים is only stylistic. אביי explains that the desert counted as רשות הרבים only when the Jewish people camped there. Next, the גמרא asks why the ברייתא spells out the punishments for carrying. It answers through איסי בן יהודה's statement in רב's hidden scroll, which is reread to mean that one unknown מלאכה lacks the full punishment, so the ברייתא tells us הוצאה is not that one. Finally, a משנה calls a valley רשות היחיד, which seems to contradict the ברייתא's ruling that it is a כרמלית. עולא answers that 'private' there just means 'not public,' and רב אשי begins a second answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's method for carrying on a public road
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה finishes his ruling: a person with houses on both sides of a public road may put up a לחי or קורה at each end and carry in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He may put] a לחי on this side and a לחי on that side, or a קורה on this side and a קורה on that side, and then carry back and forth in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא. רבי יהודה is finishing his ruling that symbolic markers at both ends of a public road let a person carry there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לחי (side post) or קורה (overhead beam) is the standard fix for a מבוי (alleyway). רבי יהודה applies the same fix even to a real public road. In his view, these symbolic markers turn the road between them into a private area.

keyTerms.meaning: A post set at the side of an alleyway's entrance that acts as a symbolic wall
A beam laid across the top of an alleyway's entrance that acts as a symbolic marker
Literally 'lifts and gives'; here it means carrying objects back and forth
In the middle, meaning between the two markers

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this road is a small alleyway. It is a real רשות הרבים, and that is exactly why the חכמים will object.

phrases.english: a post from here, and a post from here,
phrases.notes: One לחי at each end of the road

phrases.english: or a beam from here and a beam from here,
and he carries and places [objects] in the middle.
phrases.notes: Carrying is permitted between the markers

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a לחי or קורה at each end of a public road permits carrying between them.

steps.title: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's method
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that a רשות הרבים cannot be made into a carrying area with symbolic markers like these.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You cannot make an עירוב for a public domain this way!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים respond to רבי יהודה and turn down his method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, a לחי or קורה works only for an alleyway. It does not work for a true public road, which needs real walls. So the area between the markers stays a public domain.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not make an עירוב (a joining that permits carrying)
The public domain
In this way

phrases.english: They said to him:
One may not make an eiruv for the public domain in this way!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה's ruling
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using a לחי or קורה for a true רשות הרבים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Symbolic markers are not strong enough to change the status of a public road
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, a לחי or קורה cannot turn a true רשות הרבים into an area where carrying is permitted.

steps.title: Why is the private domain called 'full-fledged'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא added the word 'גמורה' when it described the רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they call it 'full-fledged'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a word in the ברייתא. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא had said 'זו היא רשות היחיד גמורה'. The word 'גמורה' seems unnecessary, since a private domain is simply a private domain. The גמרא wants to know what extra lesson it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: And why?
They called it
Full-fledged, complete

phrases.english: And why did they call it 'full-fledged'?
phrases.notes: This refers to the ברייתא's רשות היחיד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the extra word 'גמורה' teach?

steps.title: 'Full-fledged' teaches that the חכמים disagree even about throwing
steps.stepSummary: Without the word, we might think the חכמים agree that the area is a רשות היחיד for throwing. The word 'גמורה' teaches that they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: when the חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה and say the area is not a רשות היחיד, that is only about carrying inside it. But about throwing into it, they agree with him. So the ברייתא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'גמורה' blocks a mistaken idea. The mistake would be that the חכמים treat the area as private when it comes to throwing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a true, 'full-fledged' רשות היחיד counts as private. That means the area between the markers is not private even for the איסור of throwing into it from public property. So the חכמים reject רבי יהודה completely, not only in part.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
They disagree
To carry within an area
To throw from one domain into another
They agree
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, the area between symbolic markers on a public road is not a רשות היחיד in any way, neither for carrying nor for throwing.

phrases.english: What would you have said?
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא sets up the wrong idea you might have had.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: When the Sages disagree with Rabbi Yehuda
[saying] that it is not a private domain,
that applies only to carrying [within it],
but regarding throwing [into it], they agree with him;
phrases.notes: In this mistaken view, the area would be private by Torah law for throwing

phrases.english: therefore it teaches us [otherwise].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'גמורה'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'גמורה' teaches that the חכמים do not treat the area as a רשות היחיד even for throwing

steps.title: What does 'This is the public domain' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's emphatic phrase 'זו היא רשות הרבים' and asks what it comes to leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: 'This is the public domain.' What does this come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another phrase in the ברייתא and asks what its emphasis excludes. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'זו היא' ('this is') suggest that only the places listed count as a רשות הרבים. The גמרא wants to know which case is being excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: The master said (introduces a quote from the ברייתא)
This is (an emphatic, limiting phrase)
What does it come to exclude?

phrases.english: The master said:
'This is the public domain.'
What does it come to exclude?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: ״זוֹ הִיא רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים״. לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about a different line of the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case does 'זו היא רשות הרבים' exclude?

steps.title: It excludes רבי יהודה's other ruling
steps.stepSummary: The emphasis excludes a different opinion of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the other ruling of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the phrase is aimed against another ruling of רבי יהודה. The next step quotes that ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא wants to reject a view of רבי יהודה that would treat an area as public just because many people walk through it. Which view this is will be shown from a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one

phrases.english: To exclude the other [ruling] of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase excludes רבי יהודה's other ruling

steps.title: The source: the public path through the wells
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about posts around wells (פסי ביראות). רבי יהודה says a public path running through them must be moved aside; the חכמים say it need not be.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says, if a public path cuts through them, he must move it to the sides. The חכמים say he does not need to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that shows what רבי יהודה's 'other' ruling is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, people walking through cancel the private status that the posts create, so the area becomes public again. The ברייתא's 'זו היא' sides with the חכמים: only the listed places are a רשות הרבים, and a path through the wells is not one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Cuts through them, interrupts them
He must move it to the sides
He does not need to

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'them' refers to the posts around wells (פסי ביראות). The פסים are not mentioned in this text, but the משנה is about them.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיְתָה דֶּרֶךְ רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מַפְסַקְתָּן —
phrases.english: If a path of the public domain cuts through them,
phrases.notes: Through the posts around the wells

phrases.english: he must divert it to the sides.
And the Sages say: He need not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the answer in step 6

steps.title: Why is the public domain also called 'full-fledged'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא also used the word 'גמורה' for the רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they call it 'full-fledged'?
steps.whatsHappening: The same question is asked again, this time about the רשות הרבים. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רשות היחיד, 'גמורה' taught a real lesson about throwing. For the רשות הרבים, there seems to be no matching lesson, so the גמרא asks why the word appears.
steps.confusionAlert: The question has the same wording as step 3, but it is about a different line of the ברייתא: the רשות הרבים, not the רשות היחיד.

phrases.english: And why did they call it 'full-fledged'?
phrases.notes: This refers to the ברייתא's רשות הרבים

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same question as step 3, now applied to the רשות הרבים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'גמורה' add for the רשות הרבים?

steps.title: The word is just stylistic consistency
steps.stepSummary: Since the first part (רישא) said 'גמורה', the last part (סיפא) said it too. No new law is taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the first part taught 'full-fledged', the last part also taught 'full-fledged'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word in the סיפא carries no new lesson. It only matches the wording of the רישא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the standard 'איידי' answer: not every word must teach something new, because sometimes a text keeps parallel wording. The real lesson of 'גמורה' stays with the רשות היחיד.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (introduces a stylistic explanation)
The first part of the text
The last part of the text

steps.whatToRemember: 'גמורה' in the רשות היחיד line teaches a law about throwing. In the רשות הרבים line it is only there to match the wording of the רישא.

phrases.english: Since he taught the first clause [with] 'full-fledged',
he also taught the latter clause [with] 'full-fledged'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word in the סיפא is stylistic, matching the רישא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The repeated word in the סיפא teaches no new law; it only keeps the wording parallel.

steps.title: Why Not List the Desert as a Public Domain Too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges our ברייתא: another ברייתא counts the desert (מדבר) as רשות הרבים, so why did ours leave it out?
steps.simpleTranslation: And let it also count the desert! For it was taught in a ברייתא: What is a public domain? A main street, a large plaza, open-ended alleyways, and the desert!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different ברייתא includes the desert in its list of public domains. So why did our ברייתא leave it out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא listed only streets, plazas, and open alleyways as רשות הרבים. A second ברייתא adds מדבר to that same list. Two sources seem to disagree about whether a desert is a public domain.

keyTerms.meaning: Desert, wilderness
A main road or highway
A large public plaza or square
Alleyways open at both ends to public streets

phrases.english: And let it also count the desert,
for it was taught in a baraita:
What is the public domain?
A main street and a large plaza,
and open alleyways, and the desert!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's list of public domains after the side discussion about the word 'גמורה'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's list of public domains, which leaves out the desert
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel ברייתא includes מדבר, so our ברייתא's list looks incomplete or contradictory.

steps.title: אביי: It Depends on the Time Period
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the desert was a public domain only when the Jewish people lived there. Today it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is not difficult. Here (the ברייתא that lists the desert) refers to the time when the Jewish people lived in the desert. Here (our ברייתא) refers to nowadays.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. Each ברייתא is talking about a different period of history.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What makes a place רשות הרבים is that crowds actually use it. When the Jewish people camped in the desert, it was full of people. Today it is empty, so it no longer counts.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the standard opening of an answer)
Dwelling, encamped
Nowadays, in the present time

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רשות הרבים depends on how a place is actually used by the public, not only on what kind of terrain it is.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult,
here it is at the time when Israel dwelt in the desert.
Here it is at this time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by time period (כאן וכאן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות disagree about whether a desert is a public domain.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are correct. The desert was רשות הרבים in the era of the wilderness camp, but it is not today.

steps.title: Why Teach That an Accidental Carrier Brings a חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא about punishments for carrying, and asks why it states something so obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If he carried out or carried in by mistake, he must bring a חטאת. If he did it on purpose, he is punished with כרת and stoning. That he must bring a חטאת for doing it by mistake is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of the ברייתא, which lists the punishments for carrying between domains on שבת. It asks why the ברייתא needed to say that someone who does it accidentally brings a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that breaking שבת by mistake requires a חטאת offering. So it seems the ברייתא is wasting words by saying it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', a formula for quoting a line from a ברייתא already cited
Doing a sin by mistake, without knowing
Doing a sin on purpose
A sin-offering brought for an accidental sin
Spiritual 'cutting off', a punishment from Heaven
It is obvious! (a challenge that something did not need to be said)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: אִם הוֹצִיא וְהִכְנִיס בְּשׁוֹגֵג —
phrases.english: The Master said: If he carried out or carried in unwittingly —
he is liable to a sin-offering,
intentionally — he is punishable by karet, and is stoned.
Unwittingly he is liable to a sin-offering — that is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אִם הוֹצִיא וְהִכְנִיס בְּשׁוֹגֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the ברייתא now that the list of domains has been explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a שוגג brings a חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a basic, well-known law, so why does the ברייתא need to state it?

steps.title: The Real Point Is the On-Purpose Case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really needed to teach the on-purpose case (כרת and stoning). It mentioned the accidental case only to complete the picture.
steps.simpleTranslation: It needed to teach that one who does it on purpose is punished with כרת and stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the important part of the ברייתא is the on-purpose case. The accidental case was added just to round out the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's real teaching is about the מזיד, who gets כרת or stoning. Once it was listing punishments, it also mentioned the obvious שוגג case for completeness.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach this)
Is stoned by בית דין

phrases.english: Intentionally, punishable by karet and stoned —
that is what he needed to teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמֵזִיד עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת וְנִסְקָל אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of step 12 by moving the ברייתא's focus to the מזיד case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifting the focus of the teaching to a different clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is pointlessly teaching the obvious חטאת law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The real teaching is the מזיד punishment. The שוגג case is mentioned only for completeness.

steps.title: But the On-Purpose Case Is Also Obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the on-purpose punishments are also obvious, since the תורה states them openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the previous answer. The punishments of כרת and stoning for breaking שבת on purpose are written in the תורה, so why would the ברייתא need to teach them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה clearly says that one who breaks שבת on purpose is punished with כרת or death. So moving the focus to the מזיד case still leaves the ברייתא teaching nothing new. The question is now stronger than before.

keyTerms.meaning: This too

phrases.english: That too is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא needed to teach the מזיד punishments
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These punishments are written in the תורה, so stating them adds nothing.

steps.title: רב's Hidden Scroll and the Opinion of איסי בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is teaching something new, linked to רב's report of a hidden scroll. In it, איסי בן יהודה says that there are 39 main מלאכות and that one is 'liable only for one.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to teach us like רב, for רב said: I found a hidden scroll in the house of רבי חייא, and written in it was: איסי בן יהודה says, the main categories of forbidden labor are forty minus one, and he is liable only for one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not just repeating the תורה. It is teaching a point connected to an unusual statement of איסי בן יהודה, found in a hidden scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי בן יהודה's words 'he is liable only for one' are unclear. At first they seem to mean that someone who does all 39 מלאכות brings only one חטאת. The ברייתא's spelling out of the punishment for carrying builds on איסי's statement (כדרב). It does not argue against him. Step 17 explains what איסי really means, and step 18 shows what the ברייתא adds.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
A hidden scroll (private notes of Oral Torah teachings)
The main categories of forbidden labor on שבת
Forty minus one, that is, 39

steps.confusionAlert: Don't decide yet what 'אינו חייב אלא אחת' means. The simple reading (only one חטאת for all 39 מלאכות) is about to be challenged.

phrases.english: This teaches us in accordance with Rav,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב: מָצָאתִי מְגִלַּת סְתָרִים בֵּי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: as Rav said: I found a hidden scroll in the house of Rabbi Ḥiyya

phrases.aramaic: וְכָתוּב בָּהּ: אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: and written in it: Isi ben Yehuda says:
The primary categories of labor are forty less one,
and he is liable only for one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן כִּדְרַב, דְּאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by linking the ברייתא to the teaching of איסי בן יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tying the ברייתא to a disputed outside opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא only repeats punishments written in the תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא makes a point connected to איסי בן יהודה's unclear statement about liability for the 39 מלאכות.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יוחנן Says Each מלאכה Gets Its Own חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the simple reading of איסי בן יהודה's words using רבי יוחנן. He says the משנה counts 39 to teach that one who does all of them in one lapse of awareness brings a separate חטאת for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But we learned in the משנה: The main categories of forbidden labor are forty minus one. And we discussed it: Why do I need the count? And רבי יוחנן said: To teach that if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions איסי בן יהודה's statement as it was read so far. רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה says the opposite: each מלאכה brings its own חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's number 39 seems unnecessary, since the list of labors is given anyway. רבי יוחנן explains that the number teaches that each מלאכה is counted separately, even if a person did them all during one period of forgetting. This contradicts reading 'liable only for one' as 'one חטאת for all of them.'

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (introduces a challenge)
Why do I need the number?
One lapse of awareness (one period of not knowing)
For each and every one

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוחנן's rule, that each אב מלאכה brings its own חטאת even in one העלם, is a basic principle in the laws of שבת. It forces the גמרא to reread איסי בן יהודה's statement.

phrases.english: Is that so?! But didn't we learn:
The primary categories of labor are forty less one.
And we discussed it: Why do I need the count?
And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
that if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness —
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement of איסי בן יהודה brought in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of איסי בן יהודה's words 'ואינו חייב אלא אחת'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן reads the משנה's number 39 as teaching a separate חטאת for each מלאכה, which contradicts 'only one חטאת.'

steps.title: Rereading איסי בן יהודה's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes how we read איסי בן יהודה. He means 'he is not liable for one of them,' not 'he is liable only for one.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: he is not liable for one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי יוחנן's challenge by reading איסי בן יהודה's words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן proved that each מלאכה brings its own חטאת, so 'liable only for one' cannot be right. The new reading says that one of the 39 מלאכות does not get the full punishment of סקילה and כרת. We just do not know which one it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (read the text this way)
He is not liable
One of them (one of the 39 מלאכות)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say a person may do one of the מלאכות. It only says that one מלאכה has a lighter punishment than סקילה, and we do not know which one.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is fixing the wording here, so read the line this way instead.

phrases.english: He is not liable for one of them.
phrases.notes: When we don't know which מלאכה it is, that one מלאכה doesn't bring סקילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16's challenge from רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: איסי meant a person is liable for only one מלאכה in total.
steps.terutzMaskana: איסי meant that one of the 39 מלאכות, we do not know which, does not carry the full punishment of סקילה.

steps.title: What the ברייתא was teaching about carrying
steps.stepSummary: Since one מלאכה is uncertain, the ברייתא teaches that הוצאה is not that one. It is surely punished with כרת and סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what it teaches us: this one (carrying) is among those that are not in doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally answers step 14's question about why the ברייתא had to say that carrying on purpose gets כרת and סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of איסי, each מלאכה could be the unknown one with the lighter punishment. So the ברייתא tells us that הוצאה is certainly not that one. This explains why the line is not obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (the new point)
They are in doubt
Carrying from one domain to another

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's line about כרת and סקילה for carrying is needed. Without it we might fear that carrying is the one uncertain מלאכה with a lighter punishment.

phrases.english: And this teaches us:
This one is among those that are not in doubt.
phrases.notes: Carrying surely carries כרת and סקילה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reading from step 17 to close the question from step 14
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הוצאה is clearly one of the מלאכות punished by כרת and סקילה.

steps.title: The ברייתא's list of places that are neither domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. A sea, a valley, a colonnade and a כרמלית are neither רשות היחיד nor רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: But a sea, a valley, a colonnade, and a כרמלית are neither like a private domain nor like a public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the ברייתא. It is setting up a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These places are in a middle category called כרמלית. They are not fully private and not fully public. The next step will question whether a valley really belongs on this list.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting the ברייתא)
A valley or open field
A colonnade, a covered row of pillars
A middle domain, neither fully private nor fully public

phrases.english: The Master said:
But a sea and a valley
and the colonnade and the כרמלית
are neither like the private domain
nor like the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sea, a valley, a colonnade and a כרמלית are all in the middle category of כרמלית.

steps.title: Challenge: a משנה calls a valley a private domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a valley can be a כרמלית. A משנה in טהרות calls it רשות היחיד for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a valley really neither private nor public? We learned in a משנה: a valley in the summer is a private domain for שבת and a public domain for טומאה. In the rainy season, it is a private domain for both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's claim about a valley by quoting a משנה that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts a valley in the middle category. The משנה calls it רשות היחיד for שבת all year round. It only changes in summer for טומאה, when many people walk there. These two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה?
Summer days
The rainy season
Ritual impurity
For this and for that (for both)

steps.confusionAlert: Domains for שבת and domains for טומאה follow different rules. For טומאה, what matters is how many people walk there. That is why the valley's status for טומאה changes with the season.

phrases.english: And is a valley neither like the private domain
nor like the public domain?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
The valley in the summer days
is a private domain for שבת
and a public domain for impurity.
In the rainy season,
it is a private domain for both!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא quoted in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that a valley is a כרמלית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in טהרות explicitly calls a valley רשות היחיד for שבת.

steps.title: עולא: the valley really is a כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: עולא says a valley is truly a כרמלית. The משנה called it רשות היחיד only to show it is not רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It really is a כרמלית. Why does the משנה call it a private domain? Because it is not a public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the contradiction by explaining what the משנה's wording really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in טהרות was not trying to give the exact שבת rules. It only wanted to say that, for שבת, a valley is not public, even when it counts as public for טומאה. So 'private' there just means 'not public,' and the ברייתא is correct that a valley is a כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (keeping the original position)
Why does it call it
Because it is not

phrases.english: עולא said:
Actually, it is a כרמלית,
and why does it call it a private domain?
Because it is not a public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means a valley is truly רשות היחיד for שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: A valley is a כרמלית. The משנה said 'private' only to mean 'not public.'

steps.title: רב אשי begins a different answer
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי starts a second answer to the contradiction about the valley. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רב אשי is about to give a different answer to the same contradiction, and his words appear on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the attribution appears here. It tells us עולא's answer is not the only one, and a second answer to step 20's challenge is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often gives a different answer at the end of a discussion

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
phrases.notes: His answer continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a second answer to step 20, alongside עולא's answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer (content follows on the next amud)
